title: Dow Surges 1,000 Points, S&P & Nasdaq Rally; Nvidia Slides Amid CEO Probe – Live Updates
body:
The U.S. equity market staged a dramatic rebound on Monday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average surging more than 1,000 points, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite each posted gains of roughly 3 percent. The rally came after a turbulent week that saw technology‑heavy indices tumble amid concerns over rising interest rates and a series of corporate scandals. Despite the overall optimism, shares of Nvidia slipped lower after the company announced an internal investigation into allegations surrounding its chief executive’s conduct.

The Dow’s leap of 1,038 points lifted the benchmark past the 38,000‑mark for the first time since early 2022, underscoring the breadth of the recovery. Blue‑chip names such as UnitedHealth Group, Home Depot and ExxonMobil led the charge, each posting double‑digit percentage gains. The S&P 500, buoyed by a resurgence in consumer‑discretionary and industrial stocks, closed at 5,292, while the Nasdaq, which had been the hardest hit by the week’s tech sell‑off, rallied 3.2 percent to finish at 13,784. Volume was robust across all three indices, suggesting that the bounce was driven by genuine buying interest rather than a fleeting technical bounce.

Analysts point to several factors that helped reverse the market’s momentum. First, the Federal Reserve’s latest policy statement signaled a more patient approach to tightening, with officials indicating that further rate hikes may be on hold pending new economic data. That dovetail with a modestly better‑than‑expected jobs report released on Friday, which showed unemployment edging down to 3.7 percent while wage growth remained moderate. The combination of a less aggressive monetary stance and a still‑strong labor market eased fears that higher borrowing costs would choke consumer spending and corporate earnings.

Second, the technology sector found new footing after the release of earnings from several heavyweight names. Apple, Microsoft and Alphabet all delivered results that beat analysts’ expectations, highlighting resilient demand for cloud services, artificial intelligence tools and premium hardware. Those results helped to dampen the sector’s earlier anxiety over valuation gaps and supply‑chain constraints. Even though Nvidia’s shares fell about 4 percent after the company disclosed an internal probe into its CEO’s alleged misconduct, the broader tech rally held firm, reflecting investors’ belief that the company’s fundamentals remain solid and that the investigation is unlikely to materially affect its near‑term growth trajectory.

Nevertheless, the market’s optimism is not without caveats. The investigation into Nvidia’s leadership comes at a time when the chipmaker is a key beneficiary of the AI boom, and any prolonged distraction could weigh on sentiment in a sector that already carries lofty expectations. Moreover, geopolitical tensions in Eastern Europe and the Middle East continue to pose risks to global supply chains and energy prices, factors that could re‑ignite volatility if they flare. Finally, the Federal Reserve’s future policy path remains uncertain; while the latest guidance suggested a pause, inflation data released later this month could prompt a surprise move, which would likely reverberate across risk assets.

Looking ahead, investors will be watching several upcoming events for clues on market direction. The U.S. Treasury Department is slated to release its quarterly report on corporate tax reforms next week, while the Federal Reserve is expected to publish its Beige Book, offering a granular view of economic conditions across the country. In addition, the earnings season is still in its early stages, with several high‑profile companies—such as Tesla, Meta Platforms and JPMorgan Chase—set to report later this month. Their results will test whether the current rally is sustainable or merely a short‑term correction after last week’s sell‑off.

In sum, Monday’s surge marks a decisive turn in a market that had been rattled by a confluence of macro‑economic and corporate headwinds. While the rebound is buoyed by encouraging policy signals and strong earnings, lingering uncertainties—particularly around Nvidia’s leadership probe and the broader geopolitical landscape—mean that the road ahead will likely remain uneven. Market participants will need to balance optimism with caution as they navigate the next wave of data and corporate disclosures.
